history.period: Founded in the 1930s by Swami Satyanand Ji Maharaj; Panipat centre active to the present
history.summary: Shri Ram Sharnam at 588 Ashram Road, Model Town, Panipat 132103 is a Hindu spiritual centre of the Ram Sharnam movement founded by Swami Satyanand Ji Maharaj (born 1861 in Rawalpindi; spent 25 years with the Arya Samaj studying Vedanta before his realization of God in the Holy Name 'RAM' at Param Dham, Dalhousie in 1925, and giving deeksha from 1928). In December 1936 he formed the Shree Ram Sewak Sangh with five disciples to spread Ram Naam; after Pitaji (Bhagat Hansraj) passed on Vyas Purnima 2000, the work continued under Pujya Rekha Ji and Pujya Krishan Ji. The Panipat centre is a temple-like sanctuary for meditation, prayer and satsang - congregation halls where devotees chant Ram Amritvani bhajans (one prayer hall was inaugurated by Swami Satya Gandhi in 1960, per a travel guide) - and runs community-service activities. The movement describes itself as a forum for genuine devotees devoted to faith in God and universal welfare, with centres across India. NOTE: 'Shri Ram Sharnam' is a movement-wide name with multiple centres (e.g. Yamunanagar, Ludhiana); this file documents the Panipat centre at Ashram Road, Model Town. town_description: Panipat is a historic city in Haryana on NH-44 (G.T. Road), about 90 km north of Delhi. It is famous as the site of the three battles of Panipat (1526, 1556, 1761) and is today India's 'Textile City' and 'City of Weavers', the biggest centre for quality blankets and carpets.
